questions.stem: During interphase, a cell's DNA content doubles. Why is this step essential before mitosis can occur?

options.text: So the cell has extra DNA to use as energy
So each daughter cell receives a complete copy of the DNA
So the chromosomes become visible under a microscope
So the cell can produce more mitochondria

questions.explanation: DNA replication during interphase ensures that each chromosome is copied. When the cell divides during mitosis, one copy goes to each daughter cell, so both receive a complete set of genetic information. Without replication, daughter cells would only have half the required DNA.

questions.stem: Cancer cells divide much faster than normal cells. Which phase of the cell cycle is most likely shortened in cancer cells?

options.text: The gap phases (G1 and G2) of interphase
Cytokinesis only
The S phase (DNA replication)
Telophase

questions.explanation: The gap phases (G1 and G2) are the longest parts of the cell cycle and include checkpoints that normally regulate whether a cell should divide. In cancer cells, these checkpoints fail and the gap phases are shortened, allowing the cell to progress through the cycle faster and divide uncontrollably.

questions.stem: A cell has a total cycle time of 24 hours. It spends 22 hours in interphase. What percentage of the total cell cycle is spent in mitosis and cytokinesis combined?

options.text: About 92%
About 50%
About 8%
About 22%

questions.explanation: Time in mitosis + cytokinesis = 24 - 22 = 2 hours. Percentage = (2/24) x 100 = approximately 8.3%. This shows that cells spend the vast majority of their time in interphase, growing and preparing for division, rather than actually dividing.

questions.stem: A scientist adds a chemical that prevents DNA replication to a culture of dividing cells. What would happen to the cell cycle?

options.text: Cells would be stuck in G1/S phase and unable to proceed to mitosis
Cells would divide normally but produce smaller daughter cells
Cells would skip straight to cytokinesis
Cells would die immediately

questions.explanation: DNA replication occurs during the S (synthesis) phase of interphase. If this is blocked, the cell cannot complete interphase and will be unable to enter mitosis because it has not duplicated its chromosomes. The cell cycle would be arrested, which is a strategy used by some anti-cancer drugs.

questions.stem: During interphase, in addition to DNA replication, organelles such as mitochondria also increase in number. Why is this important?

options.text: So organelles can be shared between the two daughter cells after division
So the parent cell can move faster
So the cell wall becomes thicker
So the nucleus can grow larger

questions.explanation: When a cell divides, its contents (including organelles) are shared between the two daughter cells. If organelle numbers were not increased before division, each daughter cell would have too few organelles to function effectively. Increasing mitochondria ensures each new cell has enough for energy production.
